Extended analysis · Age structure

Older populations push crude rates up for chronic conditions and down for social and mental-health measures

Crude prevalence reflects who lives in a county; age-adjusted prevalence removes that, for fair comparison. The gap between them is a window on each county's age profile.

How to read
Gap > 0: adults older than the 2000 U.S. standard population, so the crude rate exceeds the age-adjusted rate.

The age-gap index is the mean z-score of the gap over eight age-graded measures (arthritis, high blood pressure, CHD, COPD, high cholesterol, cancer, hearing and mobility disability); their gaps correlate at a median of 0.97, so the index tracks one county-level age structure factor. Compare counties with age-adjusted rates; crude rates are closer to local caseload.

Source: CDC PLACES County Data (GIS Friendly Format), 2025 release, dataset i46a-9kgh; cleaned and validated project table. Model-based small-area estimates; county-level, descriptive, not causal. All project views
